summary: Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling, endurance credit rests on the already-approved 41080184 meta-analysis context (VO2max ES 0.32, time to exhaustion ES 0.38, time-trial ES -0.40). Its 2026-10-26 clinical review is unchanged; only scoring_eligible is set true, with a limitation citing the ruling. The 15256690 acute trial was read as an abstract only and stays non-eligible. Applicability now points to 41080184, requires a rosavin-standardized label (per the fourth ruling set: credit only where the product matches the studied preparation), and excludes energy, mood and anti-inflammatory claims. The record-level hold is lifted with a notes sentence, and the 41080184 reference's scoring_eligible=false flag is removed.

record_updates.notes: The signed limited endurance scope is retained. PMID15256690 reports acute200mg Rhodiola rosea (3%rosavin/1%salidroside) one hour before exercise with a small positive time-to-exhaustion result in24volunteers; its chronic200mg/day four-week phase in12volunteers was null. Full PMID30450257 reports600mg/day for four weeks in26men, with no TTE/VO2peak benefit. Review41080184 pools other species, combination products and isolated salidroside; it is retained as noncontributing history rather than an exact generic-rosea qualification. Actual227946 has205mg/capsule with3%rosavins/1%salidroside and morning directions; exact acute regimen correspondence is unestablished. Product241941 has a different marker specification. Existing required_form_terms is OR and cannot prove both specifications simultaneously. Source-purpose/preparation/regimen qualification remains held; no new signature, efficacy threshold, global inefficacy finding or safety penalty is created. Dr. Pham's signed 2026-10-28 ruling grants moderate conditional endurance credit from the 41080184 synthesis (no energy, mood, anti-inflammatory or disease claims; only where the product matches the studied preparation) and resolves the former record-level scoring_eligible=false hold.

references_structured.title: The effect of Rhodiola rosea supplementation on endurance performance and related biomarkers: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references_structured.notes: Scoring hold resolved by Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling (moderate conditional endurance credit from this synthesis).

references_structured.title: Acute Rhodiola rosea intake can improve endurance exercise performance.

applicability.studied_population: Healthy exercise cohorts; review reports26trials668participants. Table2 includes adolescents/young adults and older trained adults, heterogeneous training status. Not patients selected for mood,stress-related fatigue or inflammatory disease.

population.description: Healthy exercise cohorts; review reports26trials668participants. Table2 includes adolescents/young adults and older trained adults, heterogeneous training status. Not patients selected for mood,stress-related fatigue or inflammatory disease.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review/meta-analysis; full Methods,Results,Tables and Discussion independently inspected2026-10-27.

outcomes.name: Time-trial performance,time to exhaustion and VO2max: pooled statistically significant small endurance effects.
IL6 and CRP: no statistically significant pooled reduction.

limitations: Table2 contains RR plus Cordyceps preparations,isolated salidroside/rhodioloside,decoctions and extracts; these cannot be treated as chemically equivalent single-ingredient standardized extracts.
Source Table1 adult18–50eligibility conflicts with included adolescent cohorts; record the inconsistency rather than rewriting the population.
Exploratory subgroup>600mg/day is not a minimum effective dose; Table4 has obvious unrelated LL-BFR/HLR caption and duplicated MDA subgroup labels. No quantitative benchmark extracted.
No mood,clinical stress-fatigue,longevity,cognitive-acuity or anti-inflammatory transfer.

Current labels227946and241941 explicitly claim physical endurance; cannot exclude the entire25label cohort as non-endurance. Their exact preparation/dose correspondence remains required,not resolved by a name match.

Included-study PMID list records only13 explicit PubMed IDs printed in source bibliography;13 other source-table reports use DOI,local journals or theses. This is not a claim of26independently verified PubMed trials. Repeated Noreen/Parisi reports require trial-family mapping before independent-count claims.

Scoring eligibility set by Dr. Pham's signed 2026-10-28 ruling: moderate conditional endurance credit from this synthesis (VO2max ES 0.32, 95% CI 0.12-0.52; time to exhaustion ES 0.38, 0.07-0.69; time-trial ES -0.40, -0.78 to -0.01; Results, Table 3). Conditional on products matching the studied R. rosea preparation; no energy, mood, anti-inflammatory or disease claims. The mixed-species/combination limitations above still apply.

dose.administration_frequency: Trial-specific daily or acute protocols; no common schedule assigned.
co_therapies: Trial-specific background therapy/training and comparator; Table2 inspected; no common co-therapy assumed.
dose.reported_regimen: Table2 has acute3mg/kg regimens,170mg extract28days,600mg extract28–30days,RR+Cordyceps and other heterogeneous protocols. No single pooled regimen or equivalent marker dose is asserted.

source_provenance.location: Full Methods,Results,Tables1–3andDiscussion; exact trial-level restrictions retained.

identity.name: Rhodiola rosea extract standardized to 3% rosavin + 1% salidroside, 200 mg (with 500 mg starch)

population.description: Young healthy volunteers: 24 in the Phase I acute crossover; 12 in the Phase II 4-week phase.

study_contexts.study_design: Phase I: double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized crossover, acute dose 1 hour before testing, 5-day washout. Phase II: double-blind placebo-controlled 4-week daily intake (n=12).

dose.administration_frequency: Single 200 mg extract dose 1 hour before testing (Phase I); 200 mg/day for 4 weeks in Phase II.
dosage_forms: oral extract with starch (physical form not reported in the abstract)
co_therapies: Placebo was 700 mg starch; no co-therapy reported.
dose.reported_regimen: 200 mg R. rosea extract (3% rosavin + 1% salidroside) plus 500 mg starch, acute 1 h pre-exercise; Phase II 200 mg/day for 4 weeks.

normalization.basis: Extract mass as stated in the abstract; no marker-equivalent conversion.

source_provenance.location: PubMed abstract only; no open full text found via PMC, Europe PMC, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar.

outcomes.name: Phase I acute: time to exhaustion 17.2 vs 16.8 min with placebo (p<.05); VO2peak 52.9 vs 50.9 ml/min/kg (p<.05); other measures unchanged.
Phase II: 4-week 200 mg/day intake did not alter any measured variable.

limitations: Abstract only, so no credit from this context: primary endpoint, physical dosage form and methods could not be verified.
Small effect (0.4 min) in 24 volunteers; chronic dosing was null. This trial is also included in the 41080184 synthesis, which carries the credit.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

integration_notes: 2026-10-28 integrator: require_source_label_form removed; required_form_terms kept, matching the KSM-66/Tesnor precedent. Source-only matching rejected real labels whose ingredient row resolves through the enricher.

2026-10-28 integrator: condition gate kept (supported_outcomes ['endurance'] equals the context condition). Sean's decision is that a claim-free label may earn scoped condition credit, but today the population limits (e.g. men-only, pregnancy, children) are enforced only inside this gate, so ungating via data would drop those safeguards. Claim-free scoped credit waits for the shared applicability change (no claim / aligned claim / unrelated claim / population mismatch) under /pg-scoring-change.
